name: Tier metric selector
description: Keeps the arms at least as good as the tier's held default on public evaluations (anchored minimums) and picks the cheapest and fastest of them by list price and published speed (public_metric.py); passing work per dollar on shared cases stays available as select and pick over measured arms. Role_tiers.py computes the tier of each per-call role from the same public rows (the lowest tier unless the next tier up shows a significant gain on the evaluations of the role's kind) and applies the owner's hard constraints after; a deep-run role takes the cheapest tier whose recorded pass rate on the deep-work cases meets the sufficiency bar (sufficient_tier), and choose_tier, escalate and sub_agent_choice resolve a person's tier (current request, then standing guidance through the StandingTierGuidance port), a one-rung per-task escalation with a recorded reason, and a sub-agent's own default.
advantages: Free, offline and deterministic, with the weights, their reasons, the public numbers and their dates in data files.
disadvantages: Only as good as the public numbers (one aggregator supplies every scored number) and the owner's minimums and weights; a leaderboard revision moves the ranking until the rows are refreshed.
